text:
maya: Hey team, Terraform apply against eu-gpu-pool workspace is hung on state transfer. CI says 'error acquiring remote state lease' and the runner is blocked for 45m. Anyone seen blob lease sticky like this before?
ben: Ugh. Was there a manual `terraform state mv` or import in the middle of the run?
maya: alex kicked off a cross-account state move earlier to consolidate eu workspaces -> may have overlapped with the schedule. infra-bot: [CI] pipeline #4921 failed: workspace-lock-error (see https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/4921) :warning:
alex: yeah i initiated `terraform state mv` to split resources out of legacy workspace. I aborted once I saw drift but CI kept trying to use the old backend.
sam: do NOT force-unlock yet if there might be an active import. If there's an ongoing azure lease active, breaking it could corrupt concurrent ops.
ben: quick check: list lease status via az cli:```bash
az storage blob lease show --container-name tfstate --name eu-gpu.tfstate --account-name redwoodstate
```
ben: if it's 'leased' by a PID we don't recognize, we can `lease break` but prefer to find the job first.
maya: CI job is offline, runner shows 'terminating' on GH Actions. runner id 8912. maybe the lease holder is stale.
sre-oncall: I can correlate runner 8912 with the agent that held the lease. Give me 10m. Also pinging platform to check for stuck storage ops. :phone:
alex: I left a terminal open at home with the import command, could be me. i think it timed out but didn't release.
sam: If it's confirmed stale, do this sequence: 1) note current lock id 2) snapshot blob 3) lease break 4) run `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` from a safe env. Example commands:```bash
# snapshot before breaking lease
az storage blob download --container-name tfstate --name eu-gpu.tfstate --file /tmp/eu-gpu.tfstate.snap --account-name redwoodstate
# break lease
az storage blob lease break --container-name tfstate --blob-name eu-gpu.tfstate --account-name redwoodstate
# force-unlock in terraform state backend
terraform force-unlock -force 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
ben: also check for concurrent `terraform apply` in the other region; we saw a pattern where apac applies retried and grabbed the lease.
maya: thanks, prepping snapshot now. tagging @sre-oncall and @sam.
sre-oncall: Confirmed runner 8912 lost heartbeat 50m ago. Lease holder is a stale GUID. I backed up the blob to /mnt/backups/eu-gpu-1900123456.snap. Proceed with break.
alex: that's me — i started an interactive import then had a laptop crash. sorry, go ahead.
sam: I'll run the break and force-unlock now, then requeue the CI job. If anything weird, i'll roll state back from the snapshot and contact infra team.
maya: :thumbsup: thanks everyone, this unblocks the gpu-pool provisioning.
infra-bot: [deploy] eu-gpu-pool: re-run requested by sam (run https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/4922)
sam: requeue done, watching logs. If the apply errors, we will rollback and open a short postmortem on procedural gaps for state-moves.
maya: noted — let's add a checklist to the wiki: import -> snapshot -> scheduled quiet window -> release. Short-term runbook will save future incidents.
ben: agreed. small follow-up: add a GitHub Actions check to mark workspaces as 'maintenance' so CI won't auto-trigger during manual state ops.
maya: created a todo in infra board. closing thread once CI green.
